keyTakeaways: The earliest known print use of the trick-or-treat call is "tricks or treats" in an Ontario newspaper on 1 November 1917, a decade before the 1927 Alberta reports most quizzes cite.
The heaviest pumpkin record moved twice in a year: 1,278.8 kg on 6 October 2025, then 1,295.8 kg (2,856 lb 12.8 oz) on 3 October 2026, so 2023-era quiz answers are out of date.
No one was burned at Salem: 19 people were hanged in 1692 and Giles Corey was pressed to death.

faqs.question: What are some good Halloween trivia questions for adults?
faqs.answer: Myth-busters work best with adults, because they reward people who think they already know the answer. Ask how many people were burned in the Salem witch trials (none; nineteen were hanged) or when trick-or-treat first appeared in print (1917, in Ontario).

faqs.question: What are easy Halloween trivia questions for kids?
faqs.answer: Pick questions with a number or a name they can guess: which US state grows the most pumpkins (Illinois), how many bat species drink blood (three), or what is found beside Ichabod Crane's hat (a shattered pumpkin). Skip questions about executions for children under 8.

faqs.question: When was trick or treat first used?
faqs.answer: The earliest known print use is "tricks or treats" in The Sault Daily Star, Sault Ste. Marie, Ontario, on 1 November 1917. The 1927 Alberta newspaper reports often called the first are a decade later.

faqs.question: What is the heaviest pumpkin ever grown?
faqs.answer: As of 13 October 2026, Guinness World Records lists Ian Paton's "Bagheera" at 1,295.8 kg (2,856 lb 12.8 oz), weighed in Wargrave, UK, on 3 October 2026. The record changes most autumns, so check it again before you play.

faqs.question: When is the next full moon on Halloween?
faqs.answer: NASA's moon-phase tables put the next one on 31 October 2039 at 22:36 Universal Time. In India that is already 04:06 on 1 November, and the last full moon on Halloween was in 2020.

faqs.question: Were the Salem witches burned at the stake?
faqs.answer: No. Nineteen people were hanged in 1692, fourteen women and five men, and Giles Corey was pressed to death for refusing to enter a plea. Burning was not the punishment used at Salem.

faqs.question: How many Halloween trivia questions do I need for a party?
faqs.answer: Two rounds of six is enough for a short game, and all 30 questions here fill about half an hour at roughly a minute a question, which is our estimate. A longer league night needs a bigger bank.

faqs.question: How do I make sure my trivia answers are correct?
faqs.answer: Check each answer against the record it comes from, such as a museum page, a government statistic or the book itself, rather than another quiz list. Re-check anything that can change, like world records, every October.

faqs.question: When is Halloween in 2026 and 2027?
faqs.answer: Halloween is 31 October every year. It falls on a Saturday in 2026 and a Sunday in 2027.

faqs.question: Can SubhSandesh run a Halloween quiz for my group?
faqs.answer: No. Its two Halloween templates are greeting pages for one person, with photos, a letter and a "Will you be my boo?" question, and they do not score teams or invite guests. Use them afterwards for the winner or for someone who could not come.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Halloween Trivia Questions With Answers Checked Against a Source

These 30 Halloween trivia questions come in five rounds of six, and every answer was checked on 13 October 2026 against a named record, from a 1917 Ontario newspaper to the Guinness pumpkin ledger. The first six are myth-busters, and two more fix answers that ranking quiz lists still print out of date. SubhSandesh is a greeting-page site, not a quiz app: of the 5,199 pages people have built on it, 48.3% of views happen on a phone, so each question here is short enough to read aloud from one phone screen.

Below are the 30 questions and answers, a table comparing the rounds, and a hosting method based on 2024 memory research. The page ends with the cases where a different list will serve you better.

## What makes a Halloween trivia answer trustworthy?

A Halloween trivia question is a short factual question about the holiday, its customs, creatures, books or calendar, with one checkable answer. It is trustworthy when that answer can be traced to a record a player could open, not to another quiz list.

That matters because quiz answers age. One top-ranking list still gives a 2023 pumpkin weight that has been beaten twice since, and another, updated on 2 October 2026, still anchors "trick or treat" in print to Alberta in 1927. Both are fixed below.

## 30 Halloween trivia questions and answers in 5 rounds

Read each question once, allow 20 seconds, then give the answer and the one-line reason. The reasons are the part that settles arguments.

### 1. Myth-buster round: answers other quizzes get wrong

1. **When did the trick-or-treat call first appear in print?** In 1917, in Ontario, Canada. The Sault Daily Star printed "tricks or treats" on 1 November 1917, a decade before the 1927 Alberta reports of the exact wording that are usually quoted, per [etymologist Barry Popik's dated newspaper citations](https://www.barrypopik.com/index.php/new_york_city/entry/trick_or_treat/).
2. **How many people were burned at the stake in the Salem witch trials of 1692?** None. Nineteen were hanged, fourteen women and five men, and Giles Corey was pressed to death with stones for refusing to enter a plea.
3. **Is the "daddy-longlegs" a deadly spider whose fangs are too short to bite you?** No. The name is used for harvestmen, crane flies and cellar spiders, and none of them carries super-powerful venom, according to the [Burke Museum's spider myths pages](https://www.burkemuseum.org/collections-and-research/biology/arachnology-and-entomology/spider-myths).
4. **Does the average person swallow spiders in their sleep?** No. The Burke Museum's spider specialist says there are no specimens and no eyewitness accounts behind the claim.
5. **Do female black widows always eat their mates?** No. In most species that has been seen only in cages, never in the wild.
6. **How many bat species feed on blood?** Three. All three are vampire bats of the Americas, and they are the only mammals that live on blood alone.

### 2. Pumpkins by the numbers

7. **What is the heaviest pumpkin ever recorded?** "Bagheera", at 1,295.8 kg (2,856 lb 12.8 oz), grown by Ian Paton and weighed in Wargrave, Berkshire, UK, on 3 October 2026, per [Guinness World Records](https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/world-records/heaviest-pumpkin). Correct as of 13 October 2026.
8. **Whose record did Bagheera beat?** Paton's own: "Muggle", 1,278.8 kg, grown with his twin brother Stuart and weighed on 6 October 2025.
9. **Which US state grows the most pumpkins?** Illinois, with about 533 million pounds in 2025, slightly more than the next four states combined, per the [USDA Economic Research Service](https://www.ers.usda.gov/newsroom/trending-topics/pumpkins-background-statistics).
10. **Roughly how many pounds of pumpkins did the United States grow in 2025?** About 1.47 billion pounds.
11. **What are most Illinois pumpkins grown for?** Processing into purée and pie filling: nearly 70% of Illinois pumpkin acreage in the 2022 Census of Agriculture, while about 85% of US acreage overall grew fresh and decorative pumpkins.
12. **How many pounds of pumpkin were available per American in 2025?** 5.2 pounds, against a 2022 to 2025 average of about 6.

### 3. Books before the films

13. **In what year was *Frankenstein* first published?** 1818, by Mary Shelley; Project Gutenberg hosts the 1818 text.
14. **Is Frankenstein the monster?** No. Victor Frankenstein is the student who builds the creature, and the creature is never given a name.
15. **At which university does Victor study?** Ingolstadt, where he is sent at seventeen.
16. **What is the name of the ship that carries Dracula's boxes of earth to England?** The *Demeter*, a Russian schooner from Varna, in Bram Stoker's 1897 novel.
17. **What is found beside Ichabod Crane's hat in *The Legend of Sleepy Hollow*?** A shattered pumpkin.
18. **Whose ghost is the Headless Horseman said to be?** A Hessian trooper whose head was carried away by a cannonball in the Revolutionary War, as Washington Irving tells it.

### 4. Calendar and sky

19. **What day of the week is Halloween in 2026 and in 2027?** Saturday 31 October 2026 and Sunday 31 October 2027.
20. **When did a full moon last fall on Halloween?** 31 October 2020, at 14:49 Universal Time, per NASA's moon-phase tables.
21. **When is the next full moon on Halloween?** 31 October 2039, at 22:36 UT. In India that is 04:06 IST on 1 November, so Indian players can argue it misses.
22. **In which year did Harry Houdini die on Halloween?** 1926. He died on 31 October in Detroit.
23. **What does the UK mark with bonfires on 5 November?** The arrest of Guy Fawkes on 5 November 1605, guarding gunpowder beneath the House of Lords.
24. **Which Mexican festival, held from the end of October into early November, welcomes dead relatives home?** Día de los Muertos, the Day of the Dead.

### 5. Creatures and customs

25. **Do garden spiders move indoors when autumn arrives?** No. Outdoor spiders cannot survive indoors; the ones in your house are separate species, called house spiders.
26. **Do two red marks on the skin prove a spider bite?** No. Real spider fang punctures are hardly ever visible to the naked eye.
27. **Where does the common vampire bat live?** From Mexico to Argentina and Chile, in warm climates only.
28. **In which year did UNESCO inscribe Mexico's Day of the Dead on its heritage list?** 2008, after first proclaiming it in 2003, per the [UNESCO listing](https://ich.unesco.org/en/RL/indigenous-festivity-dedicated-to-the-dead-00054).
29. **Which crop's yearly cycle ends around the Day of the Dead?** Maize, Mexico's main food crop.
30. **What do families lay from the cemetery to the house to guide souls home?** Flower petals, candles and offerings.

## The 5 rounds compared

The table compares the rounds by size, where the answers were checked, and who they suit. It is the quickest way to pick two rounds for a short game.

| Round | Questions | Answers checked against | Best for |
|---|---|---|---|
| Myth-busters | 6 | 1917 newspaper citations, Burke Museum | Adults who think they know Halloween |
| Pumpkins by the numbers | 6 | Guinness (3 Oct 2026), USDA (2025 crop) | Mixed ages; numbers invite close guesses |
| Books before the films | 6 | Project Gutenberg texts of Shelley, Stoker and Irving | Readers and teenagers |
| Calendar and sky | 6 | NASA moon tables (2001 to 2100) | Groups across time zones |
| Creatures and customs | 6 | UNESCO (2008), museum and zoology records | Families with children over 8 |

The takeaway: the myth-buster and pumpkin rounds produce the most arguments, so run them first while the room is fresh. Save the calendar round for last, when a time-zone debate is welcome.

## How to host it so the answers stick

Let each answer land before you say anything else. In three versions of a [2024 experiment in npj Science of Learning](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC10948872), people remembered unrelated school facts worse when those facts came straight after a trivia question that had made them highly curious.

So keep announcements, scores and snack calls for the gap between rounds, not between questions. For the myth-buster round, ask teams to bet 1, 2 or 3 points on how sure they are; a confident wrong answer about Salem gets the loudest groan and the longest memory.

- Budget about a minute per question including the reason: two rounds take roughly 12 minutes and all five roughly 30 (our estimate).
- Keep the reasons short: one sentence, then the next question.

## After the quiz: one Halloween page for one person

The quiz is for the room. SubhSandesh's two Halloween templates are for one person, and neither runs a quiz, scores teams or invites guests. Pages built on the platform average 11.1 views each, which suggests people reopen a personal page in a way they never reopen a score sheet.

For the friend who won, or the one who could not come, the [interactive Halloween card with up to six photos](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween) takes about 5 minutes. They knock three times, carve a pumpkin until your word glows and read your letter by flashlight.

If it is your partner and you want more, the [cinematic Halloween website with a 60-second voice note](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween-premium) takes about 10 minutes, holds up to 12 photos, can stay locked until a time you set, and has a reply box for one answer of up to 280 characters. For anything that is not Halloween, the [full template gallery](https://subhsandesh.in/templates) lists every other page type.

## When this list is the wrong choice

Thirty questions is deliberate, but some games need more. A ten-round league night needs a longer bank, checked the same way.

- **Film night:** none of the 30 questions is about a film, so a movie crowd needs a film-only set.
- **Young children:** questions 2, 22 and 23 mention executions and death; drop them for under-8s.
- **Non-US groups:** the USDA questions use 2025 US figures only, not UK, Indian or Australian harvests.
- **Records move:** the pumpkin record changed on 6 October 2025 and again on 3 October 2026, so re-check question 7 before each October.

A printed sheet also beats any link when players have no phone. A SubhSandesh page is the wrong tool for the group itself, because it greets one person and has an English-only interface.

## Sources

- Barry Popik, "Trick or Treat", barrypopik.com, entry dated 18 September 2008.
- Burke Museum, University of Washington, "Spider Myths", no publication date.
- Guinness World Records, "Heaviest pumpkin", record dated 3 October 2026.
- USDA Economic Research Service, "Pumpkins: Background & Statistics", updated 29 September 2026.
- Keller and colleagues, "States of epistemic curiosity interfere with memory for incidental scholastic facts", npj Science of Learning, 18 March 2024.
- UNESCO, "Indigenous festivity dedicated to the dead", inscribed 2008.

structuralLimitations: SERP: 1 WebSearch call (US-served index), 13 October 2026. Non-spam top results: weareteachers.com (100 questions), jotform.com (300 questions, updated 2 Oct 2026, sells a quiz maker), romper.com (39 questions, Sep 2022). The rest of the top 9 were hijacked-subdomain spam (cs.grinnell.edu, vtour1.ocus.com, msoid.icmbio.gov.br, webmail.ujcm.edu.pe, calculator.icnareliefcanada.ca): 6 weak of 9. serps.md (Google, earlier) also lists today.com, rd.com, mentalfloss, greatwolf; not fetched.

BRIEF/prompt claim found false: the task prompt says "trick or treat" first print = Alberta 1927 (as in b2 history-of-halloween and b4). Barry Popik's dated newspaper citations show "tricks or treats" in The Sault Daily Star, Ontario, 1 November 1917, and "treat or trick" in the Owen Sound Sun, 2 November 1917; Wikipedia's Trick-or-treating article (fetched via API) agrees. 1927 Alberta is the earliest exact-wording citation Popik lists, not the first print use of the call.

Answers verified against fetched sources not linked in the body (to stay within 3-6 outbound links): Salem 19 hanged (Wikipedia API, Salem witch trials; UVA Salem Witch Trials Documentary Archive for Giles Corey pressed to death); three blood-feeding bat species (Wikipedia API, Vampire bat) and common vampire bat range (Animal Diversity Web, Desmodus rotundus); Frankenstein 1818, Ingolstadt, Dracula's Demeter from Varna, Sleepy Hollow shattered pumpkin and Hessian trooper (Project Gutenberg texts #84, #345, #41 and the #84 catalogue note on the 1818 edition #41445); full moons 31 Oct 2020 14:49 UT and 31 Oct 2039 22:36 UT (NASA GSFC Moon Phases 2001-2100, Espenak); Houdini died 31 Oct 1926 in Detroit and Bonfire Night 5 Nov 1605 (Wikipedia API); 2026 Saturday / 2027 Sunday (BRIEF §1, checked by calendar arithmetic). timeanddate.com, thecanadianencyclopedia.ca, etymonline, britannica, loc.gov and parliament.uk returned 403/bot walls and were not worked around.
No Halloween usage data exists in facts.md; the platform-wide phone share, page count and views-per-page lines are used as such, never as Halloween figures.

Sibling overlap: the b3 halloween-movie-trivia SERP (its brief) was a different set; this post contains no film questions. Shared 4+ URLs with no sibling named in the prompt as far as the briefs record.

auditReport.honestAssessment: An answer engine has a reason to cite this over WeAreTeachers, Jotform and Romper because it carries answers they get out of date (the 1917 Ontario print of the trick-or-treat call, the 3 October 2026 pumpkin record, NASA's 2039 Halloween full moon with the IST twist), each traceable to a named record. It is 30 questions against their 100-300 and the domain is far weaker, so it will lose head-term volume to the big lists; its realistic win is the 'is this answer right' and myth sub-queries, over months, not weeks.
